title: Hong Kong Department of Health follows up on patient data leak from Gleneagles Hong Kong Hospital mobile app
date_note: The Department of Health press release (24 Nov) is the first public statement; it says the hospital found the unauthorized activity on 18 November and notified the Department on 23 November.
geo_basis: Hospital in Hong Kong named by the Department of Health; city-level pin
summary: Hong Kong's Department of Health says Gleneagles Hong Kong Hospital found unauthorized activity affecting the security facilities of its patient mobile app on 18 November, leading to unauthorized access to some patients' personal data and other personal data. The hospital told the Department on 23 November. The Department has required the hospital to notify affected patients and submit an investigation report within four weeks. The release gives no number of patients.
plain: A Hong Kong private hospital's patient app was accessed without authorization, exposing some patients' personal data. The health authorities have told the hospital to notify those affected.
exec: The Department of Health will check whether the hospital breached the Private Healthcare Facilities Ordinance and will take regulatory action if needed.
action: The Department of Health advises that the hospital must notify all affected patients as soon as possible, and it reminds licensed private healthcare facilities to strengthen information security.

sources.name: Hong Kong Department of Health (government press release)
